title: Quagmire IV with both alphabets hidden, key of 8 (repeating, and sliding with word sum 13): exhaustive placings of the 13 clue plain letters that close the 4 loops, scored by the forced letters, best 300 completed
k4_result: Repeating key: 118,611,979 survivors (all placings of A B C E H I K L N O R S T on distinct places that close the 4 loops and keep the clue cipher letters distinct within each piece, up to shift and unit multiple). Best forced-letter score z = 5.40 over the survivor mean (top-20 mean z 5.08). Best 300 completed on the big model: best -5.498, top-20 mean -5.635, word coverage 0.38, e.g. GGHEADOMMCBYMYPEDPEGLEASTNORTHEASTFILNCPINITPILCKARLIFTHDASWHERBERLINCLOCKSDSILLALYOKUVXFUCUPISDO (noise). Sliding key, word sum 13: 52,480,393 survivors, forced z 4.70, completed best -5.135, top-20 mean -5.249, coverage 0.44 (noise). No reading reaches -5.1 (English).
controls: 3 shuffled K4s (seeds 17478, 18229, 18547), redrawn until they have K4's structure (4 loops, pieces of 11 and 3, every loop a real test): repeating key 101-127M survivors each, completed best -5.284, -5.254, -5.200 (top-20 means -5.425, -5.340, -5.293), forced z 4.43, 3.55, 4.96; sliding W=13 51-55M survivors, completed best -5.008, -5.200, -5.190 (top-20 means -5.317, -5.304, -5.309). K4 is worse than all three controls on the repeating key and inside their spread at W=13.
planted: 1/4 recovered (0/4 ranked first). Four English messages with the real clue words, random alphabets on both sides, random key of 8 (two Vigenere, two Beaufort, one with sliding W=13), redrawn to have K4's structure. True setting's forced-score rank: 82 of 134.3M (in the best 300, read back 87/97 at -4.345), 23,014 of 149.7M, 1,820,268 of 127.2M, 336,474 of 57.0M (sliding). The test lacks power: about 21 non-clue letters are forced and that is not enough to lift the true setting into the completed list in most cases.
scope_limits: THE TEST LACKS POWER: the planted answer was recovered in only 1 of 4 cases, so this is NOT an elimination of Quagmire IV at length 8. Covered: key length 8 repeating (Vigenere and Beaufort form, which are the same system here) and the sliding form with word sum W = 13 only. Sliding keys with the other 24 word sums (they reduce to W = 1 and W = 2) are not run (each costs 12 times the repeating search). Only the best 300 of the forced-letter ranking were completed; completion (annealing 13 plain letters, 12 cipher letters and the piece offset) reaches -4.7 to -4.8 on wrong settings of planted texts, so completion itself has too much freedom to judge more than the true region. The clue positions are taken as exact. Lengths 11-13, 16+ untouched.

negative.family: Quagmire IV, both alphabets hidden, key length 8
negative.hypothesis: K4 is a Quagmire IV with two freely written alphabets and a key of 8 numbers (ABSCISSA length, K3 grid width), repeating or sliding.
negative.scope: Every placing of the 13 clue plain letters closing K4's 4 loops at key length 8 with distinct places (up to shift and unit multiple, so Vigenere = Beaufort), repeating key and sliding key with word sum 13; 171,092,412 survivors scored by an order-3 chain on their 45 forced positions, best 300 completed by annealing on the big model.
negative.outcome: No signal, weak test: K4 best completed -5.498 (repeating) and -5.135 (W=13) vs shuffled controls -5.20 to -5.28 and -5.01 to -5.20; no English. Planted 1/4 recovered (true settings ranked 82, 23,014, 1,820,268, 336,474), so the idea stays open.

follow_ups: The bottleneck is the first-stage ranking (about 21 forced non-clue letters, scattered). A stronger first stage would score each survivor by a quick partial completion of only the 26 cross-piece positions (the piece offset is a 26-way choice) plus the forced letters; that adds ~10 letters per survivor at ~26x the cost, so it needs a C-speed leaf or a tighter pruning bound (branch and bound on the chain score, since every window term has a known maximum).

Sliding key at length 8 with odd or even word sums (W = 1 and W = 2 stand for all 24): 12x the repeating cost each, about 1 hour per text with 12 processes on this code; worth running only after the first stage has power.

A cheaper discriminator: the 118M K4 survivors fix the plain-alphabet places of the 13 clue letters; restrict to placings where those 13 letters read as part of a keyword alphabet (13 letters in keyword order then the rest in A-Z order). That is a small subset with a far stronger prior and would be decisive in seconds.
